title: Significance of single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) for the course and outcome of liver diseases based on clinical endpoints
summary: Many people have small differences in their genes that can influence their risk of developing certain liver diseases. Research data has shown that some of these differences are harmless, while others may increase the likelihood of liver health problems, but not necessarily. The aim of this study is therefore to find out whether and to what extent these genetic differences influence the survival time and health of the patients affected. The study will use existing data, such as laboratory values, doctor's letters and imaging results. In addition, outstanding survival data will be obtained via the Saarland Information Portal. This means that patients will not have to undergo any further procedures or examinations. All data collected will be statistically evaluated to identify differences in the diseases and their progression.

interventions.name: Retrospective-prospective cohort analysis of patients with cholestatic liver diseases who were tested for cholestasis-relevant SNPs between 2013 and 2024.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who were treated at the Clinic for Internal Medicine II at the Saarland University Hospital and underwent genetic analysis of cholestasis-relevant SNPs of ABCB4, ABCB11, ATP8B1 and NR1H4 genes between 2013 and 2024.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who do not fit into the previously defined group, with missing genetic SNP analyses or a data restriction, are excluded from the evaluation. Patients with completely missing data sets are also excluded.
